newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish couple is a family in more ways than one.
newsitem.headline: Spanish couple is a family in more ways than one.

text.p: Like many couples, they met, fell in love and had children. But there was no church wedding for Daniel and Rosa Moya Pena -- they are brother and sister.
They have been living together happily for nearly 18 years, but their relationship has only now become one of the hottest topics on the Spanish airwaves.
The town council in the northern Spanish village of Cambre voted on Wednesday to allow the Moyas and other non-traditional unions to register and gain local legal status, municipal officials said.
But Spain's central government does not approve, and legal experts say the town council's decision has no validity.
The two were separated in early childhood when their parents split. Daniel was taken by the father and Rosa by the mother. Both were later sent to separate orphanages, where they grew up.

They had no contact until they met 18 years ago in a Madrid discotheque. They started dating and fell in love. Only later in their courtship, did they discover they had more than a family name in common.
After the shocking discovery, the couple briefly broke off their relationship. "But we couldn't stand being apart for more than six months," Daniel told reporters.
They came to consider themselves a married couple and had two children, now 11 and 5.
Spain does not recognize common-law marriages. Incest is one of the country's strongest social taboos.
But the Cambre municipality, which lies in the Galicia region, has opened a new registry for all unions, including those between blood relatives or between more than two people.

Miguel Cortizo, a regional official, told the Spanish newspaper El Pais that he considered the decision a good one but said "some well-intentioned people are going to say they are legalizing sexual perversion."
Many callers to Spanish radio and TV talk shows voiced support for the Moyas, but others condemned them and called their relationship a remnant of Spain's dark past.
